Takeaway #1 - Roles should focus on the persona, not the domain • This is already something we've been thinking about with regards to new roles in the future, but it was still validating to hear that Ramp thinks about roles in the same way. The main question they ask when creating a role is "what access does this person need to do their job?"

Takeaway #2 - The importance of hierarchy when it comes to permissions and permissions-like systems • Ramp has both roles and workflow-specific approvers, but they have a clear hierarchy in that roles and permissions live above any specific payment policies implemented, in order to avoid conflicts between a role someone is assigned to, and an approval workflow someone has created • This is much less clear on Carta today - we have permissions, assignment logic and designated approvers - and each can take a different priority depending on the workflow, which is something I'd argue we should standardize and clarify (for ourselves and our users)
